Lessons.Title: Multiplication Practice (optional)
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 IM Grade4 U01 L04 is an optional multiplication-within-100 fluency lesson. The existing Edulytics original introduction and goal remain intact; original 2021 teacher preparation, lesson and 2-page student statements were checked.

Activity1 15 min: sort original multiplication fact cards into 'know right away', 'can find quickly' and 'don't know yet', choose precisely five facts to practise, share personal strategies; teacher reviews confidence sorting.

Activity2 20 min: source Find the Number Stage1 game on a 1–36 board: chooser claims a number and its score; opponent claims only currently uncovered factors and sums their values. Alternate; no uncovered factors means lost next turn. Finish when no factor moves remain; highest score wins. Teacher supervises material and scores, not claimed auto-graded.
Lesson synthesis 10 min: multiplication fact strategies and mathematical-community norms.

Edulytics original 5-minute Cool-down, user-approved NOT original publisher text: using 10×6=60 and 3×6=18 explain 13×6=78, and show a strategy for an additional challenging multiplication fact. Teacher assesses reasoning; numeric Practice checks products separately.

KeyConcepts.Title: Distributive multiplication
KeyConcepts.Definition: Use familiar facts to compute a harder multiplication product.

KeyConcepts.Title: Self-assessment
KeyConcepts.Definition: Choose facts that are recalled or derived at different speeds.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Select 5 challenging facts for targeted practice.
KeyConcepts.Example: Sort into three personal confidence piles.

KeyConcepts.Title: Factors game
KeyConcepts.Definition: Two-player game with a 1–36 board and covered factors.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Only uncovered divisors score for the other player.
KeyConcepts.Example: Choose 9: get 9 points, opposing side gets 1+3=4.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find the Number example
WorkedExamples.Question: Chooser chooses 9, factors 1 and 3 remain uncovered. What are the scores?

WorkedExamples.Title: Independently authored Grade 4 lesson reasoning
WorkedExamples.Question: How can 14×7 be solved using the distributive property?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the exact relationship and representation requested by this lesson.
WorkedExamples.Check: First-party mathematically checked model. Original publisher activity and student drawings require independent teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Scoring covered factors more than once.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Covered tiles cannot earn further points.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Track covered state under teacher supervision.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating card-sorting confidence as a graded mathematics category.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Review the five selected facts with a teacher.

SummaryPoints: Original 2021 two-page student-task PDF read; source teacher lesson documents the partner Stage1 Factors game separately.
Three self-assessment categories and five facts, with discussion.
Game needs 1–36 board, currently uncovered divisors, alternation and scoring, teacher-supervised.
Cool-down is first-party Edulytics with source-equivalent skill; publisher original unseen.
